notes:
Account summary
- Prospect is cost-sensitive, high-volume summarization. They currently run large batch jobs summarizing customer calls, support tickets, and internal docs.
- Theme across calls: they want aggressive cost reduction, but only if quantization is “safely scoped” and reversible per workload.

Workload / technical notes (from discovery + deep dive)
- Primary workload: summarization (async) with large daily volume.
  - “We can tolerate slower p95 on the batch lane if it halves our token bill.”
  - Peaks: nightly / end-of-week backlogs.
  - Traffic shape: many medium-length prompts; completion length varies; occasional long-context docs.
- Secondary workload: interactive triage (daytime) where latency matters.
  - They do NOT want quantization enabled here initially.
  - Concern is customer-facing “weirdness” and formatting regressions.
- Output constraints:
  - Some routes require strict JSON output (internal schema validator). They have seen quantization cause subtle formatting drift with other providers.
  - They asked if Redwood can keep quantization off for JSON-mode/tooling routes while enabling it for “free-form” summaries.

Key requirements (what they keep repeating)
- Route-scoped quantization enablement:
  - Must be able to enable quantized path ONLY for background summarization routes.
  - Wants a canary percentage control at route level (start 1–5%, ramp up).
  - Wants a rapid kill switch (disable per route, ideally immediate / minutes, not hours).
- Quality guardrails:
  - Wants a clear published regression threshold and what signals will auto-disable.
  - They asked for: baseline vs quantized comparison on their own prompt set (“bring your own eval prompts”).
  - They want monitoring segmented by route and tagged by profile version.
- Unit economics:
  - They are comparing vendors on tokens/$ and $/doc.
  - Success criteria discussed: 25–40% cost reduction on summarization lane without measurable format regressions (JSON routes excluded in phase 1).
- Deployment/security:
  - Prefer VPC deployment (or Dedicated w/ isolation) due to PII in customer data.
  - Wants SSO/SAML for Console, audit logging for route config changes, and retention controls for request/response logs.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Which initial model(s) and quantization profiles are available for summarization? They are flexible on model brand, but want predictable quality and cost.
- Clarify rollback semantics: does disabling quantization flush cached artifacts immediately across workers? (They referenced past “stuck config” issues with another vendor.)
- Provide a short written explanation of precedence for toggles (org default vs customer override vs route) and how it shows up in audit logs.

POC plan (draft)
- Phase 1: Enable quantization on a single async summarization route only; exclude interactive triage and JSON-mode routes.
- Canary: start 1%, ramp to 10% after 48h if no regressions.
- FinchAI to provide:
  - Golden prompt set + expected output checks (format/schema) for their strict routes.
  - Example documents for long-context edge cases.

Internal chatter
- Markus Klein notes: “This is the cleanest fit we’ve seen for route-scoped quantization: high-volume batch lane + clear separation from latency-sensitive user-facing routes.”
- Ava Chen: push to align with Optimize beta positioning; FinchAI is a strong beta candidate if we can demonstrate quick disable + clear dashboarding.

Risks
- If they observe any JSON/tool-calling regression, they will halt POC. Strong recommendation: keep strict JSON routes unquantized until dedicated evals pass.
- Procurement will likely stall without a written rollback/runbook and an agreed-upon quality gate definition.
